claims.claim: Evagrius Ponticus was a Christian monk and ascetic who lived from 345 to 399 AD.
Evagrius left Constantinople around 382 and joined a monastic community in Jerusalem led by Rufinus of Aquileia and Melania the Elder, taking monastic vows in 383.
Evagrius then went to Egypt, where he spent the rest of his life in Nitria and Kellia until his death in 399.
The Sententiae ad monachos (Ad monachos) is a set of 137 chapters on the monastic life.
The work was written in distichs, in imitation of the Proverbs.
The work was directed probably to a monastic community in Jerusalem associated with Melania and Rufinus.
The full Greek title indicates it was addressed 'to those in cenobia or communities' (πρὸς τοὺς ἐν κοινοβίοις ἢ συνοδίαις μοναχούς).
Evagrius discusses matters foundational to the coenobitic monastic life, so the material resembles, in some ways, a rule.
The work is often associated with CPG 2436 under the designation 'The Mirrors.'
The Greek text was edited by H. Gressmann and published in Texte und Untersuchungen 39, 4 (Leipzig, 1913): 152-165.
A more recent critical edition was published by Christoph Joest in 2012 as part of Fontes Christiani 51 (Freiburg im Breisgau: Herder).
